question.text:
You are evaluating three fixed income securities based on their yield and duration: Security A: Yield = 6%, Duration = 5 years Security B: Yield = 5%, Duration = 7 years Security C: Yield = 4%, Duration = 4 years
Rank the securities based on yield-to-duration ratio (Yield/Duration).

answer.text: Cannot determine from the given data

explanation.text: The Logic: Yield-to-duration ratio = Yield / Duration. Security A: 6%/5 = 1.20. Security B: 5%/7 = 0.714. Security C: 4%/4 = 1.00. Ranking (highest to lowest): A > C > B. The Trap: Option B (B, A, C) tempts those who anchor on highest yield (6%) and highest duration (7y) without actually dividing. Option C (C, B, A) tempts those who reverse the rank. Option D is the 'giving up' trap. Cross-Exam Context: Yield, duration and their ratios are tested in NISM-VII (Securities Operations), NISM-XV (Research Analyst), and NISM-XXI-B (PMS Managers) fixed-income chapters. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Yield/Duration is essentially a 'return per unit of rate risk' lens - use it in client conversations to justify why a 6%/5y corporate bond may be a better PMS holding than a 5%/7y G-Sec even when the absolute yield gap looks small.
